name: Québec — Charter of the French Language and non-public schooling: temporary-stay exemptions, unsubsidised private schools, home schooling and CEGEP
name_fr: Québec — admissibilité à l'enseignement en anglais (Charte de la langue française)
description: Complements Agent 01's record `nat-qc-english-schooling-eligibility` (eligibility for English public and subsidised schools), which is not repeated here. This record covers what that record leaves out, from primary texts: (1) the temporary-stay exemption for children of foreign nationals with a work or study permit is set by Charter s.84.1 (enacted by Bill 96, S.Q. 2022, c.14, s.57, assented 1 June 2022): valid up to three years, not renewable, extended to 30 June of the school year; the regulation (C-11, r.7, s.7 as amended by Bill 96 s.169) applies the same three-year limit to the other temporary categories. (2) Unsubsidised private schools may teach in English, but English instruction received there by the child or a sibling is disregarded for eligibility (Bill 104, 2002). (3) Home schooling: the learning project must cover the language of instruction and the second language, one French and the other English; support from an English school board requires English eligibility. (4) CEGEP: Bill 96 caps English-language colleges' enrolment, gives admission priority to students declared eligible for English instruction, and requires all English-CEGEP DEC students to pass three courses in French and (unless eligible) the uniform French exam.

attributes.see_also: nat-qc-english-schooling-eligibility (Agent 01): general French-instruction rule, permanent eligibility via a Canadian-citizen parent, application and appeal route.
attributes.temporary_stay_exemption_foreign_nationa: Charter s.84.1 (Bill 96 s.57): 'A child who is a foreign national and who stays in Québec temporarily may, at the request of one of his parents, be exempted from the application of the first paragraph of section 72 and receive instruction in English' if (1) he holds a permit under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act that authorizes him to work or study in Canada; (2) he is a dependent child of a foreign national authorized to work or study in Canada under such a permit; or (3) he is exempt from needing the Immigration minister's consent where the parent is a temporary foreign worker or international student. 'The exemption is valid for a period of up to three years and may not be renewed. However, the exemption is extended until 30 June of the school year during which the period of validity ends if that period ends before that date.'
attributes.temporary_stay_other_categories: Regulation C-11, r.7 (made by O.C. 608-97, Gazette officielle 21 May 1997) covers holders/dependants of a Québec certificate of acceptance, Canadian citizens or permanent residents from another province, foreign representatives and Canadian Armed Forces dependants. Bill 96 s.169 replaced its s.7: 'an exemption provided for by this Regulation is valid for a period of up to 3 years', extended to 30 June. In the 1997 text the cap applied only to other-province Canadians and Forces dependants, and exemptions were renewable; Bill 96 struck the separate permit-holder categories (now s.84.1). No exemption for refugee claimants or for those receiving a Québec selection certificate (it ends on 30 June of that school year) — 1997 text s.1, para 3, as amended.
attributes.transition: Exemptions granted before 1 June 2022 that could not be renewed under s.84.1 could be renewed once, no later than 30 days before expiry, for at most one year (Bill 96 transitional provision).
attributes.consequence_for_a_permit_holder_family: English schooling on a work/study-permit basis is limited to about three school years in total and cannot be renewed; when the family becomes permanent (or receives a Québec selection certificate) the child moves to the French-instruction rule unless a parent is a Canadian citizen meeting s.73 — see nat-qc-english-schooling-eligibility.
attributes.unsubsidised_private_schools: Private schools not accredited for subsidies may teach in English to any child at full cost. Bill 104 (2002) added to s.73: 'instruction in English received in Québec in a private educational institution not accredited for the purposes of subsidies by the child for whom the request is made, or by a brother or sister of the child, shall be disregarded.' Since 2010, s.73.1 and Regulation C-11, r.2.1 allow such instruction to be weighed in a points-based assessment, but only for requests under s.73 paras 1–2, which require a Canadian-citizen parent. Practical reading: an unsubsidised English private school is a lawful fee-paying option for a newcomer child, not a route into English public schooling. The ministry's private-school layer shows language(s) of instruction but not subsidy status, so each school must be asked.
attributes.home_schooling: The homeschooling regulation does not impose French as the medium: the learning project must apply the Minister's programs 'for every compulsory subject: the language of instruction and the second language (one in French and the other in English)', mathematics, science and technology, social sciences. Home learners have the support of the school service centre (French) — support from an English school board requires the child to be eligible for instruction in English (MEQ Guide for parent-educators, 2026 edition).
attributes.cegep: Bill 96 (Charter ss.88.0.1–88.0.18): colleges are designated French- or English-language; English-language colleges' combined enrolment may not increase and may not exceed the lesser of 17.5% of total college enrolment or the previous year's share (s.88.0.5); English instruction in French colleges capped at 2% (s.88.0.6); English colleges must give admission priority to students declared eligible for English instruction when oversubscribed; every DEC student at an English college must pass at least three courses given in French (eligible students may substitute three French-language courses) and, unless eligible, the uniform French examination (s.88.0.17, in force from 2023-24/2024-25). Unsubsidised private colleges teaching in English count toward the English cap (s.88.0.13). Implication: a newcomer child schooled in French secondary will normally attend CEGEP in French; English CEGEP places are capped and prioritised for eligible students.
